WEEKLY REAL ESTATE MARKET CLOSE | 19–23 OCTOBER 2026

A challenging week for Indian real estate stocks! 🔻 The Nifty Realty index fell 5.04% to 784.35, underperforming the Nifty 50, which declined 2.36%. All 10 Nifty Realty constituents ended lower across four trading sessions.

🔻 Top 5 Realty Stock Decliners (Weekly)

Anant Raj: −10.03%

Lodha Developers: −9.04%

Aditya Birla Real Estate: −6.95%

Prestige Estates: −6.67%

Godrej Properties: −6.66%

📉 5 Stocks That Fell the Least

Sobha: −1.26%

Phoenix Mills: −1.30%

DLF: −2.67%

Brigade Enterprises: −4.89%

Oberoi Realty: −5.30%

📊 What shaped the week?

▪️ Oil and rate worries: Brent crude climbed to around $114 per barrel amid West Asia tensions, adding to inflation and interest-rate concerns.

▪️ Mixed Q2 results: Godrej Properties reported an approximately 62% fall in quarterly profit, while Sobha’s profit declined 55% and Mahindra Lifespace’s fell 66%, despite strong sales indicators.

▪️ Broader market pressure: The Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 7.27%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 declined 5.63%.

🟢 Outside the Nifty Realty index: Kolte-Patil gained 6.64% during the week, bucking the broader decline.

👀 What to watch next week: Crude oil prices, the US Fed decision, the Jio Platforms listing and upcoming real estate earnings.

videos.title: Mass Housing Is Very Difficult”: Developer Explains Why Affordable Housing Is Stuck
videos.description:
Why is affordable housing so hard for private developers to build? And could Dubai’s 48-hour rule fix it?

In this conversation about expanding from Pune into Mumbai’s western suburbs, building homes for the next 30–40 years, and what has to change for affordable housing to work in India.

🔑 Key highlights:
• ₹100 Cr+ in sales in about a year at Signature Residences, before the sales experience centre had even opened
• Prices up from around ₹40,000 to ₹52,000+ per sq ft (base price)
• Spectrum Life, Santacruz West: 30+ amenities on a half-acre-plus plot off Linking Road
• DN Nagar project overlooking a 4-acre garden, with work-from-home nooks and a rooftop infinity pool
• TREOS, their real estate operating system: vendors bid online and every purchase can be audited
• “My Opinion Matters”: 30% of buyers asked for a pet park, and it became the project’s USP
• Mumbai redevelopment strategy: society (33(7)) and MHADA (33(5)) projects, no slum redevelopment yet

🏠 On affordable housing:
Why margins are thin, why approvals and costs are unpredictable, and three fixes he suggests: deemed approvals, faster mechanised construction, and stronger rules for buyers who default (like Dubai, where the title goes back to the developer within 48 hours).

📈 What’s next:
A ₹6,500 Cr MOU with the Government of Maharashtra for a 200-acre township at Urse on the Mumbai–Pune Expressway, about 1.5 million sq ft of launches in Pune, three new redevelopment projects in Mumbai, and roughly ₹1,000 Cr+ of launches (about 2 million sq ft) planned for the next year.

videos.title: Assured Returns, Transfer Charges, QPR & More: RERA Chiefs, Builders Debate Contentious Issues
videos.description:
The R&M Podium VII brought together leading RERA Chairpersons, policymakers, developers, and industry experts to discuss the evolving regulatory landscape of India's real estate sector. The session focused on key challenges, policy updates, and reforms aimed at strengthening transparency, improving compliance, and protecting the interests of homebuyers and developers.

The discussion covered a wide range of topics, including transfer charges, delayed possession, interest rates under RERA, Quarterly Progress Reports (QPR), revised CA audit requirements, assured returns, sanction plan validity, joint development agreements (JDAs), project registration, enforcement mechanisms, and proposed amendments to the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act.

Key Discussion Points:

• UPRERA clarified that the assignment of a Builder Buyer Agreement is neither a sale deed nor a sub-lease. Therefore, no stamp duty is applicable on such assignments. Transfer charges have been capped at ₹1,000 for transfers within the family and ₹25,000 for transfers outside the family.

• Developers highlighted concerns regarding transfer charges and delayed payment interest, while regulators discussed maintaining fairness to reduce disputes and litigation.

• UPRERA explained that interest payable under RERA is linked to MCLR plus 1%, whereas consumer courts often award significantly higher rates, reinforcing the effectiveness of RERA in dispute resolution.

• Punjab RERA emphasized the need for stronger enforcement mechanisms to improve recovery of dues and ensure better compliance with regulatory orders.

• The importance of the Quarterly Progress Report (QPR) as the primary monitoring tool under RERA was discussed in detail. Developers also raised concerns over the revised CA audit reporting format, which UPRERA agreed to review with industry representatives.

• RERA Chairpersons shared recommendations for amendments to the Act, including greater clarity on the 500 square metre/8-unit threshold, flexibility in granting project extensions where delays are beyond the promoter's control, redefining force majeure, and empowering RERA authorities to issue directions to civic bodies.

• Delhi RERA and UPRERA reiterated that projects should be marketed strictly on carpet area and reaffirmed that assured return schemes are not permissible under the Act, except where specifically allowed.

• The panel discussed the relationship between sanction plan validity and RERA registration, recommending phased registration for large township projects to ensure smoother implementation and regulatory compliance.

• Developers also raised concerns regarding recent provisions affecting Joint Development Agreements (JDAs), while UPRERA explained the rationale behind revised land cost disclosures and circle rate-based valuation.

Panel Speakers:

Sanjay Bhoosreddy, Chairman, UPRERA
Anand Kumar, Chairman, Delhi RERA
Rakesh Goyal, Chairman, Punjab RERA
Parneet Singh Sachdev, Chairman, HARERA Panchkula

Under his able leadership, the Group has achieved tremendous success and Alphathum has been sold over 85 per cent in a short span of two years.

videos.title: Housing.com Group CEO congratulates Team R&M on 7th Anniversary
videos.description: Congratulations to the Realty & More team on completing seven successful years, says Dhruv Agarwala, Group CEO, Housing.com, Makaan.com, PropTiger.com. “Realty & More magazine has been a true champion of the real estate ecosystem. I wish Palash and Realty & More team many, many more years of success”, said Agarwala.

videos.title: Hope the magazine continues to provide an able platform to the sector: RICS South Asia MD
videos.description: Realty & More is doing well in the digital space during the current pandemic times, says RICS South Asia MD Nimish Gupta. Gupta wished the magazine best on the completion of its 7 years. “I hope the magazine continues to provide an able platform to the sector”, said Gupta.

videos.title: R&M celebrates 7th anniversary
videos.description:
On the completion of seven years of Realty & More magazine, Ankur Bhatiani, CEO, Urbainia Spaces congratulated the Team R&M. Bhatiani said the magazine has been providing great insights about the sector all these years.

Seven years is a great achievement, especially for a real estate magazine, says Corporate Lawyer Divya Malcolm. The Corporate Lawyer added that she is proud of the magazine and would wish the entire Team R&M all the very best. “I'm sure they will scale greater heights in the years to come”, said Malcolm.

videos.title: Gulshan Director congratulates R&M on its 7th Anniversary
videos.description: On the occasion of seventh anniversary of Realty & More magazine, Gulshan Director Yukti Nagpal congratulated Team R&M. Nagpal expressed her admiration for the magazine. The Gulshan Director wished the Team R&M best for its future endeavours.

videos.title: ‘Realty & More’, a frontrunner in getting information on regulatory reforms: C&W
videos.description: Congratulations to Team R&M on completing seven glorious years, says Shalin Raina, Managing Director- Residential Services, Cushman & Wakefield. Raina said thanks to the magazine for bringing information, especially pertaining to the regulatory reforms the industry is going through right now. “I wish you all the best for the future, keep shining”, said Raina.

videos.title: ‘Realty & More’ has been a frontrunner in providing information: Signature Global Chairman
videos.description: Real estate sector attracts a lot, but there are few who provide true information related to the sector, says Pradeep Aggarwal, Chairman, Signature Global. The Signature Global Chairman said ‘Realty & More’ is one such magazine which provides accurate and correct information of the industry. “Many congratulations on the seventh anniversary and wish all the best for future endeavours”, said Aggarwal.
